clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether the new DIV and MOD, the new word to address conversion and the new EXP byte count compute the old words, read in the library sources the lock pins (ruint 1.21.1, alloy-primitives 1.7.3).
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched arithmetic.rs at evm2 7c9f3b6d and e80df9c4 and diffed them. Only lines 22 and 32 differ, as the unit says. In e80df9c4 interpreter/stack.rs:12 defines Word as U256, and the WordExt trait in utils.rs:29-66 declares no checked_div or checked_rem, so the calls resolve to ruint. ruint v1.21.1 src/div.rs:9-14 and :36-41 return None for a zero divisor and otherwise Some(self.div(rhs)) and Some(self.rem(rhs)). src/macros.rs impl_bin_op maps Div and Rem to the delegate named at div.rs:149-150, which is wrapping_div and wrapping_rem, the routines the old text called. bits.rs defines byte_len as bit_len().div_ceil(8), so EXP gas is unchanged. utils.rs to_address is Address::from_word((*self).into()). The words that UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14) and simpleMulDiv (:26) receive are therefore the same, a zero divisor still gives 0, and PoolManager.unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) is untouched by this change.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Live read-only eth_call of a DIV and MOD stub placed by state override on Ethereum and Tempo, bracketed with web3_clientVersion.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran my own stub independently at 2026-11-27T16:58Z. It returns eight words: DIV and MOD of 2^256-1 by 0, DIV and MOD of 2^256-1 by 2^255+12345, DIV and MOD of a 201-bit dividend by a divisor with a nonzero top limb, and DIV and MOD at Z-1 and 5Z. Both reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc (ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com) and tempo/v1.19.2-c0c9372 (rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz) gave the reference words for all eight. This checks the old evm2 revisions only, which is what the unit claims. No public endpoint runs e80df9c4.

clearedSpotChecks.check: callers.py rerun on tempo main and reth main: no production caller starts a transaction while a user transaction runs.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched tempo main crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs and read the two Tempo entries the unit lists. Lines 474-515 (settle_storage_credit_refunds) take the transient storage of STORAGE_CREDITS_ADDRESS after a successful message and leave other addresses' transient slots alone. Lines 520-565 run execute_system_call only when the envelope is a system transaction, and that call is the transaction itself, not a nested one. A public account cannot reach that path. crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs:234-245 marks a system transaction by the fixed TEMPO_SYSTEM_TX_SIGNATURE with zero gas, value and nonce. crates/transaction-pool/src/validator.rs:524-525 rejects system transactions from the pool, and block.rs:617 and :671 validate them separately during block execution. The callers list in out/callers_tempo_main.txt has no PRODUCTION transact inside a precompile. Tempo also carries opcode overrides in crates/evm/src/instructions.rs (a millisecond timestamp that stops existing at T1C, and an SSTORE with TIP-1060 storage credits that writes only STORAGE_CREDITS_ADDRESS state besides the normal store). Neither is a nested transaction, and the PoolManager bytecode has no TIMESTAMP, per OPCODES.md:146. The clear_transaction_state effect the unit derived by reading would bypass src/PoolManager.sol:112 if a caller ever appeared, so the lead to rerun callers.py on each release is warranted.
